content: Hello! how can I help today?
I’m self-employed—should I prioritize a SEP IRA or a Solo 401(k)?

You can combine both for maximum benefit:
1. Use **SEP IRA** to make employer contributions up to ~20% of your adjusted net earnings.
2. Then fund a **Solo 401(k)** salary deferral—up to $22,500 in 2024 (or $30,000 if 50+).
This maximizes deduction and retirement savings in the same year.
Yes. The SEP goes on **Schedule 1**, Line 16; Solo 401(k) contributions are shown on **Schedule 1**, Line 19. Keep detailed records to allocate between the two plans.
Any filing requirements for the Solo 401(k)?
Only if the plan’s assets exceed $250,000—you’ll need to file **Form 5500-SF**. Otherwise, no annual filing requirement besides including contributions on your return.
